item.title: Conjoined twins recovering well after successful separation in Saudi Arabia
item.description: The mother of the conjoined twins, Akeneta Rokobati Tacaqe who were successfully separated in Saudi Arabia, says she is overjoyed to see her babies recovering well after the operation, describing the moment they were separated as precious. Speaking to fijivillage News, Tacaqe says the twins spent five days in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit before being transferred to the general ward.
item.content:encoded:
The mother of the conjoined twins, Akeneta Rokobati Tacaqe who were successfully separated in Saudi Arabia, says she is overjoyed to see her babies recovering well after the operation, describing the moment they were separated as precious.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Tacaqe says the twins spent five days in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit before being transferred to the general ward.

She says the babies were initially placed in separate rooms before doctors moved them into one room two days later.

Tacaqe says the twins no longer require oxygen, are breathing well and have started taking food after being on milk for a few days.

She says the family had been waiting for this moment for several months and were initially nervous while watching the operation live, but later became more comfortable.

Tacaqe says she is particularly happy to see her babies separated and thanked the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for making the operation possible.

She says the family wanted to give twinsÂ Jesipeli and Di Cecea Kikau Â an additional Arabic name Sara and Noura as a way of showing their appreciation to Saudi Arabia for what it has done for them.

Tacaqe also praised the medical staff for their expertise, care and kindness, saying they looked after the family very well throughout their hospital stay.

She says the support from families in Saudi Arabia who regularly visit them has also made them feel at home away from home.

Tacaqe says her family back home is overjoyed and cannot wait to meet the babies.

She hopes to bring the twins back to Saudi Arabia one day to show them where they were separated.

She also hopes the children may one day consider working in the medical field as doctors or nurses so they can give back to the community and help others.

Tacaqe thanked everyone who has kept her family in their thoughts and prayers, saying the babies are doing well and their return to Fiji has not yet been decided as they are still recovering.

item.title: Drains are not rubbish bins – Nasinu Town Council
item.description: The Nasinu Town Council is urging residents and businesses to stop dumping rubbish into drains, warning that blockages can cause flooding and create unhealthy living conditions during heavy rain. The Council says its operations team is carrying out drain-cleaning work across different wards in Nasinu, removing rubbish, debris and other materials obstructing water flow.
item.content:encoded:
The Nasinu Town Council is urging residents and businesses to stop dumping rubbish into drains, warning that blockages can cause flooding and create unhealthy living conditions during heavy rain.

The Council says its operations team is carrying out drain-cleaning work across different wards in Nasinu, removing rubbish, debris and other materials obstructing water flow.

The Council says blocked drains can lead to flooding, stagnant water, unpleasant odours and unhealthy conditions for families living nearby.

Residents are being reminded that drains are not rubbish bins and should not be used to dispose of household waste, plastics, bottles or grass cuttings.

The Council says while its workers continue clearing drains, residents and businesses must also take responsibility by disposing of their rubbish properly.

The Council stresses that keeping communities clean and safe is everyone's responsibility.

The Nasinu Town Council is encouraging everyone to work together to keep drains clear, maintain a clean environment and reduce the risk of flooding during heavy rain.

item.title: 33-year-old man charged with three counts of sacrilege in Ba
item.description: A 33-year-old man from Varavu, Ba, who was arrested in connection with alleged sacrilege cases in the Ba area, has been charged. The man has been charged with three counts of sacrilege and six counts of breach of order of suspended sentence.
item.content:encoded:
A 33-year-old man from Varavu, Ba, who was arrested in connection with alleged sacrilege cases in the Ba area, has been charged.

The man has been charged with three counts of sacrilege and six counts of breach of order of suspended sentence.

He is alleged to have unlawfully entered three temples and stolen religious statues, which were later found damaged.

The accused is expected to appear at a special court sitting in the Ba Magistrates Court today.

The man from Varavu, Ba, broke into a temple in Rarawai on 5th November and stolen a religious statue.

The statue was later found in pieces in a nearby creek.

item.title: Kamikamica stresses unity, respect and understanding this Diwali
item.description: Respectful dialogue, consideration of different perspectives and a commitment to every Fijian's dignity are essential as Fiji continues its constitutional review. This is the message from Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce and Business Development Manoa Kamikamica in his Diwali message.
item.content:encoded:
Respectful dialogue, consideration of different perspectives and a commitment to every Fijian's dignity are essential as Fiji continues its constitutional review.

This is the message from Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce and Business Development Manoa Kamikamica in his Diwali message.

Kamikamica says this year's theme, "One Fiji, One Light: Building Understanding, Respect and Unity", reminds Fijians that despite their different faiths and traditions, they share common hopes for peace, opportunity and a better future.

He says Diwali's message of understanding and goodwill is particularly important as the country continues its constitutional review.

Kamikamica says these values also reflect Fiji's economic aspirations, stressing that prosperity must mean more than material wealth and should create secure livelihoods, dignified work and opportunities for families to progress.

He says the Government continues to strengthen entrepreneurship and economic participation through business support, co-operative development and training, particularly in rural and maritime communities.

Kamikamica says Diwali celebrates the triumph of righteousness over evil, knowledge over ignorance and light over darkness.

He also highlights the significance of the return of Lord Rama, Sita and Lakshmana to Ayodhya, while the blessings associated with Goddess Lakshmi, Lord Ganesha and Goddess Saraswati represent prosperity, wisdom, knowledge and new beginnings.

On behalf of his family and the Ministry, Kamikamica extends Diwali greetings to Hindu families in Fiji and abroad, and hopes the festival brings peace and happiness while inspiring all Fijians to treat one another with kindness and respect.

item.title: Singh family celebrates Diwali with prayers, sweets and family gatherings
item.description: Diwali festival serves as a reminder of the victory of good over evil, light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance. This was revealed by Shagrika Shayal Singh of Nawaicoba, Nadi, saying Diwali commemorates the return of Lord Rama, Mata Sita and Lakshman to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile, following Lord Rama's victory over Ravana.
item.content:encoded:
Diwali festival serves as a reminder of the victory of good over evil, light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance.

This was revealed by Shagrika Shayal Singh of Nawaicoba, Nadi, saying Diwali commemorates the return of Lord Rama, Mata Sita and Lakshman to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile, following Lord Rama's victory over Ravana.

She says she celebrated Diwali by visiting the temple with her husband before visiting her parents' home, where friends also came over to share sweets and spend time together.

Singh who is celebrating her first Diwali with her in laws says she helped her mother-in-law prepare sweets for the celebrations, with the two staying up until 11pm despite her work commitments.

She says the celebrations also included sharing snacks, catching up with friends, taking photographs and making TikTok videos.

Singh says the family also planned to offer prayers, light diyas and set off firecrackers, which are her husband's favourite part of the celebrations.

However, she is urging Fijians to be considerate when setting off firecrackers, particularly around young children and household pets who may be frightened by the loud noises.

Singh says she personally dislikes firecrackers because her dog gets frightened by them.

She is wishing all Fijians a happy Diwali and encouraging everyone to celebrate safely while being mindful of others.
